 Chainsingh And Others

sentences.text: Shri Mohd. Rafik Sheikh, learned counsel for the ap  Shri Vijay Gulani appearing on behalf of Shri Vindh  Khare,learned counsel for the respondent No.3.

This misc. appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 14.01.2019 in MACC No.116/2015 passed by MACT, Badwani for enhancement of Rs.10,00,000 compensation regarding death son of appellant No.1 &2 and brother of the appellant No.3.
2.

Facts in brief are that a claim under Section 166 of the MACT, 1988 was preferred seeking Rs.22,50,000/- compensation for the death of Sanjay Singh born on 02.03.1985 (Ex.P/128) who succumed to injuries caused in motor accident dated 28.03.2015 at 10:30 pm at Satpura Colony,
near Girls College, Badwani under the jurisdiction of PS Badwani (M.P) due to negligent driving of motorcycle scooter No. MP 46 MH 0353 driven by 2 MA-2234-2019 respondent No.1, owned by respondent No.2 and insured by respondent No.3.

It was also stated that deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month through private tuition and was under treatment from 20.03.2015 to 27.03.2015 and expenses of Rs.1,50,000/- were incurred in his treatment but he died on 27.03.2015.
All the applicant/petitioners were dependents of the deceased.
3. Respondent No.1 and 2 did not contested the case but respondent No.3 contested the case.
Tribunal confirmed the issues and recorded the testimony of Chain Singh as PW-1, Ramjay Chouhan as PW-2 and admitted the docments Ex.P/1 to P/136 on behalf of the applicant/petitioners.

Respondent No.3 examined Nimesh Trivedi as DW-1 and Sub Inspector Chain Singh as DW-2 and adduced the documents Ex.D-1 to D-17.
4.

Appreciating the evidence Tribunal appreciated that death of Sanjay Singh was due to bodily injuries incurred due to negligent driving of motor scooter driven by respondent No.1, owned by respondent No.2 and insured by respondent No.3.

A total compensation of Rs.6,93,000/- with 7%
interest payable from 18.09.2015 the Tribunal awarded the compensation in the following heads:-

1  (1) Loss of dependency : Rs.4,68,000/-

sentences.text:
( 2) Funeral Expenses : Rs.15,000/-
 (3) Loss of Estate : Rs.15,000/-
 (4) Medical Expenses : Rs.78,000/-

Total Compensation : Rs.6,93,000/-
5.

This appeal has been preferred on the ground that income of the 3 MA-2234-2019 deceased has been assessed on lower side ignoring the fact that deceased was a computer operator and the deduction in personal expenses is incorrect considering the family environment.
The increase in future prospect ought to have been awarded 50%.

The multiplier ought to have been applied 18,
medical expenses ought to have been awarded as per the actual expenses of Rs.1,50,000.
6. Counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company opposed the prayer.
Heard and perused the record.
7. Tribunal has disclosed the income of the deceased in para 25 of the award and has assessed the income Rs.6,000/- per month.

As per Ex.P-130 Sanjay Chouhan passed a 3 years degree course of B.A. on 01.05.20214 in second division from Madhya Pradesh Bhoj (OPEN) University, Bhopal and he passed the shorthand and typing examination from M.P Government vide certificate Ex.P-129.

He obtained various certificates in proficiency in computer applications vide Ex.P-13, P-132 and also participated in sports events vide Ex.P-135 and initially obtained an appointment letter during his study vide Ex.P-133.
He completed data entry operator course from Government Polytechnic College, Barwani vide Ex.P-125.
Accordingly, the future prospect assessed on the date of 22.03.2015 is on lower side.
Considering the bright future of the deceased the future income of the deceased including the future prospect is assessed as Rs.10,000/- per month.
8. His date of birth as mentioned in Ex.P-124(C) was 02.03.1985 and his death occurred on 11:30 am of 27.03.2015.

Accordingly, he was 30 year 4 MA-2234-2019 0 months 25 days old and applicable multiplier for the age group of 26 to 30 years, as he has not completed the age of 31 years he was only in the running age of 31.
Therefore, applicable multiplier would be 17 and on re-calculation of loss of dependency it comes to Rs.10,20,000/- (10,000- 50% for personal expenses = 5,000 x 12 = 60,000 x 17 = 10,20,000).
Tribunal has awarded only Rs.4,68,000/- , therefore, a compensation of Rs.5,52,000/- is enhanced in the head of loss of dependency.
Tribunal have not awarded in the head of loss of consortium.
Accordingly, Rs.80,000/- is awarded in the head of loss of consortium.

The amount in the medical expenses does not require interference as no bill has been rejected but considering the duration of treatment from 22.03.2015 to 27.03.2015 in Suyash Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Indore the transportation expenses, loss of earning of the parents ought to have been awarded and in this head a total of Rs.30,000/- is also awarded.
Accordingly, a total compensation of Rs.6,62,000/- is further enhanced with interest at the rate of 7% from the date of application i.e 18.09.2015.
The enhanced amount shall be disbursed and satisfied as per para 31 of the award.
With the aforesaid, this misc. appeal stands disposed of.
